diagram_math_checks.evidence: The figure lies in R^2 with a=1/sqrt(iota(2)), u=(a,a) as defined in Example. Both dashed circles have centre (0,0) and radius iota(2); def-p-norms-on-rn identifies the 2-norm with the Euclidean norm, and def-canonical-natural identifies iota(2) with the real scalar 2.

The coordinates s0=(0,0), s1=(1,0), s2=(1,-1), s3=(1+a,a-1), s4=(a,a-1), s5=(a,a), s6=s0 match Example and Verification 2.1 exactly. The six explicit directed segments have differences e0,-e1,u,-e0,e1,-u, in order. The last segment is explicitly s5--s0 and is visibly present in the native output. There are six distinct vertices and six directed edges, each vertex having one incoming and one outgoing path edge; the unmarked crossing of segments is not an additional partial-sum vertex.

Cumulative addition of e0,e1,u,-e0,-e1,-u gives t0=(0,0), t1=(1,0), t2=(1,1), t3=(1+a,1+a), t4=(a,1+a), t5=(a,a), t6=t0. These are precisely the coordinates and six directed segments in the right panel. The explicit last segment t5--t0 is visibly present. Six distinct vertices and six directed edges form a closed oriented path.

Verification 3.1 and 4.1 give good squared norms 0,1,2,3,2-sqrt(2),1,0, all below 4. Verification 1.3 and 2.2 give ||t3||^2=3+2sqrt(2)>4. Independent coordinate arithmetic also gives ||t4||^2=2+sqrt(2)<4. The native panels visibly put all good vertices inside the circle and t3 outside. No optimal-constant or sharpness claim is added.

The complete original Example, Facts, and all 13 Verification steps are a byte-identical prefix of the successor. Caption explicitly says the norm comparisons are established independently of the figure. No argument cites the new picture.
